hero.title: Paste without being asked
hero.description: iOS asks every time UniClip reads something you copied in another app. Allow it once and syncing stays quiet.
hero.emptyClipboardHint: Copy some text in another app first. iOS skips the prompt when the clipboard is empty.
hero.triggered: Prompt requested. If it appeared, tapping Allow Paste is all it takes.

prompt.title: “UniClip” would like to paste from “Notes”
prompt.message: Do you want to allow this?

fallbackSection.header: No prompt, or tapped Don’t Allow?
fallbackSection.footer: The Paste from Other Apps row only appears after UniClip has asked once. iOS doesn’t tell apps which option you chose, so there’s nothing to confirm back here.

findApp.title: Find UniClip in Settings
findApp.description: Open the Settings app, go to Apps, and tap UniClip. Open iOS Settings below jumps straight there.
findApp.tip: On iOS 17 and earlier, UniClip sits near the bottom of the main Settings list.

openPaste.title: Tap Paste from Other Apps
openPaste.description: It’s in the Allow UniClip to Access list and usually shows Ask.
openPaste.tip: Row missing? iOS adds it only after UniClip has asked once. Close this and tap Show the prompt first.

chooseAllow.title: Choose Allow
chooseAllow.description: UniClip can now read what you copy in other apps without asking. It takes effect right away.
chooseAllow.tip: iOS doesn’t tell UniClip which option you picked, so there’s no confirmation to wait for.
